name: Ishita Dasgupta
bio: My graduate research is focused on leveraging microfluidics to establish an organoid model of colorectal cancer.

name: Jaime Greatorex
bio: My graduate research uses microfluidics to investigate how gut microbes shape the development of intestinal organoids, how the gut microbiome shapes the function of the small intestine epithelium, and what conditions are needed to determine the spatiotemporal dynamics within a group of bacterial species.

name: Liya Patel
bio: My research focuses on building a control system to assess liver function in microfluidic liver devices.

name: Diana Brizzolara
bio: My goal is to design and test microfluidic devices that allow passive spatial control of oxygen, generating localized gradients through oxygen diffusion using PDMS layer geometry.

name: Kyla Narayan
bio: My project uses a physics-informed neural network to model 2D oxygen diffusion in a tissue scaffold.

name: Julia Gerber
bio: My project involves building and testing microfluidic devices for bacterial chemotaxis.

name: Katerina Muchacho
bio: My project explores how different growth environments and spatial orientations affect bacterial growth, with a focus on how these conditions influence bacterial quorum sensing and communication.

name: Tengis Munkhbat
bio: My current goal is to build a control algorithm that improves the predictive validity of liver-on-chip systems by simulating pharmacokinetics in silico under hepatotoxic conditions.

name: Dominique Orbea
bio: My project focuses on the genetic modification of bacteria via transformation with a fluorescent reporter plasmid, the study of bacterial surface attachment under static and flow conditions, and the design of a new vector.
